subject: Tiered GPU procurement ops & cloud backstop — ACME deal tie to capacity
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@nvidia.com>, CloudOps Team <cloud-ops@cloudia.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tiered GPU procurement ops & cloud backstop — ACME deal tie to capacity

Carlos / CloudOps —

Quick summary: ACME (deal ACME-6742) has signaled a committed go-live window tied to the end of Q3. They want a predictable Dedicated capacity plan (initial 160 A100-equivalent vCPUs) with a staged onramp. Given OEM lead times, we need a hybrid plan: a short-term cloud-reserved backstop + staggered OEM shipments.

As we finalize commercials, can you do two things by EOD Tuesday: 
- Carlos: confirm the OEM quote lead times for the SKUs in the attached PDF and whether OEM will accept a two-tranche PO (50% now / 50% on a 60-day milestone). If partial shipments are possible, indicate earliest partial-ship ETAs and any minimum order constraints.
- CloudOps: provide a 90-day reserved-node holdback estimate and cost delta to give ACME an option to burst to cloud for months 1–2. Include any SLA/credit language you need us to request from the customer.

Attachments: OEM_quote_Q3_v2.pdf (pdf) — vendor quote we received last week; cloud_capacity_snapshot-May22.csv — our current reserved pool availability by region.

Why this matters: ACME is requesting a canary window starting 2026-09-15; if OEM shipments slip beyond mid-September we need to confirm cloud bridge economics so the customer’s onboarding timeline isn’t affected.

Next steps: I’ll consolidate replies into a mutual action plan draft and share with ACME procurement.

Thanks,

Soojin Lee
Manager, Strategic Accounts (Sales Ops)
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: OEM_quote_Q3_v2.pdf (pdf, 482KB)]
[Attachment: cloud_capacity_snapshot-May22.csv (csv, 64KB)]

From: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@nvidia.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, CloudOps Team <cloud-ops@cloudia.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 24 May 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tiered GPU procurement ops & cloud backstop — ACME deal tie to capacity

Soojin —

Thanks for the clear breakdown. Per the attached quote (OEM_quote_Q3_v2.pdf) here’s what we can commit to today: 
- Lead time: current manufacturing slot for the quoted A100-equivalents is ~11–13 weeks from PO receipt (subject to final configuration).
- Partial shipments: we can do a two-tranche PO with a 40/60 split; minimum first tranche is 40 units. Partial shipments will incur a $750 per-unit split handling fee and may shift the overall fulfillment window by ~1–2 weeks depending on line scheduling.
- Priority lane: for an incremental premium (roughly 6% uplift on hardware list), we can move ACME into a prioritized manufacturing lane that targets a 9–10 week fulfillment horizon. That requires a signed PO within 7 business days.

I’ve included our commercial rep (Carlos Vega) and a brief PDF summary attached. If you want, we can mark Tentative Ship Week windows once PO milestone dates are firm.

Regards,
Carlos Vega
Enterprise Sales — OEM Partnerships
NVIDIA
[Attachment: OEM_quote_Q3_v2.pdf (pdf, 482KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Tiered GPU procurement ops & cloud backstop — ACME deal tie to capacity

Forwarding Carlos’s note — good detail. Two quick internal asks: 

1) Cost/Timing trade: we should map three lanes in the MAP draft: (A) aggressive OEM priority (sign PO within 7 days for 9–10 week ETA), (B) standard OEM two-tranche (11–13 weeks, 40/60 split, split fee), (C) cloud-reserved backstop (immediate but higher run-rate). I’ve pulled ballpark cloud delta numbers and will drop them into the MAP draft.

2) Onboarding impact: if shipments land closer to 13 weeks, our onboarding milestone (canary 2026-09-15) is at risk. We need a commitment from CloudOps on the duration/cost for a 60-day bursting plan and any required SLA credits to give ACME confidence.

Marissa — FYI on potential impact to onboarding schedule and kickoff resourcing. If OEM wants the 6% premium lane, we should confirm whether the customer (ACME) will accept the uplift vs paying more for cloud bridging.

Ben
Director, GTM Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@nvidia.com>, CloudOps Team <cloud-ops@cloudia.io>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Acme AI Purchasing <acme-ai-purchasing@acmeai.com>
Date: Wed, 27 May 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tiered GPU procurement ops & cloud backstop — ACME deal tie to capacity

Thanks Carlos — and thanks team. I’ve drafted a short mutual action plan (MAP) structure below and attached an editable workbook. Please review and flag any missing milestones or commercial conditions by EOD Friday. Once we align internally I’ll send to ACME for signature.

Proposed MAP lanes (high level):
- Lane A (OEM priority): sign PO within 7 business days -> NVIDIA prioritized lane -> target ship weeks 9–10 -> 6% OEM premium -> partial-shipment allowed (min 40 units)
- Lane B (Standard OEM two-tranche): sign PO -> 11–13 week window -> 40/60 split, $750 split handling fee -> tentative ship weeks assigned after PO
- Lane C (Cloud backstop): reserved nodes in us-west for 60–90 days -> immediate availability -> cost delta = $0.18/token-equivalent (approx) additional run-rate; include SLA credits equal to 5% of monthly reserved fee if capacity not available within 24 hours of scheduled burst

Milestones to capture in workbook: PO dates, invoice milestones, tentative ship week, partial-ship acceptance, cloud-reserved hold window, canary start (2026-09-15), full prod start (2026-10-15), DocuSign delivery link, HubSpot deal update.

Requests: 
- Carlos: can you confirm whether NVIDIA can accept DocuSign with the two-tranche PO terms and whether the split handling fee is negotiable at scale? Also please provide a tentative ship-week table for both Lane A and Lane B (so we can put solid dates in the MAP).
- CloudOps: please confirm the 60-day holdback cost and the SLA credit language we can present to ACME (copyable clause recommended).

I’ve attached the draft MAP: mutual_action_plan-draft.xlsx. I’ll consolidate changes and aim to route to ACME procurement next week.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head, Dedicated Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: mutual_action_plan-draft.xlsx (xlsx, 72KB)]
